question: A drug trial of 1,500 people sees no liver failure. By the rule of three, what is the highest plausible rate, in cases per 1,000?
move: Seeing nothing in a small group only rules out the common.
ask: What have I decided is safe just because nothing went wrong the few times I tried it?
trap: Zero, because nothing at all happened to anyone in the trial.
hint: With nothing seen in a group, the upper limit is about three divided by its size.
steps: Rule of three: upper limit is about 3 ÷ people watched
reference: Hanley & Lippman-Hand, If nothing goes wrong, is everything all right? Interpreting zero numerators, JAMA, 1983
